question: Which three sacraments imprint an indelible spiritual 'character' and therefore cannot be received more than once?

choices.C: Confirmation, Matrimony, and Anointing of the Sick

teaching.title: The Sacramental Character
teaching.body: Baptism, Confirmation, and Holy Orders each imprint an 'indelible spiritual mark' (character) on the soul — a permanent configuration to Christ that cannot be erased. This is why they may never be repeated. The character is not about worthiness or moral state; even a lapsed Catholic retains their baptismal character. This doctrine explains why priests who leave ministry retain their ordination and why 'conditional baptism' rather than rebaptism is used when there is doubt about a previous baptism.
